A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same shared-Q-network pretraining work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original offline-RL experiments, representation-rank and frozen-backbone analyses, and additional online-RL experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original offline-RL experiments and appendix analyses, and adds proxy Q-error results and expanded visual-benchmark results.

M1.justification: The central transition-pretraining followed by Q-learning procedure is unchanged. However, v2 removes two substantive methodological extensions from v1 Appendices A–B: online pretraining with collected or pre-existing data, and continuous joint training with L_Q = L_TD + L_dynamics instead of a separate pretraining phase.

E1.justification: V2 removes the online SAC/TD3 evaluation regime covering six Gym MuJoCo tasks in v1 Appendix A. Conversely, visual evaluation expands from Walker Walk and Cheetah Run on medium and medium-expert datasets to include Humanoid Walk and medium-replay datasets in Table 3. The other offline benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The online SAC and TD3 comparisons disappear with v1 Appendix A. V2 also supplies previously missing AWAC medium-replay and IQL random/expert comparisons in retained tables. The principal offline comparator families remain unchanged. V1 inconsistently names its visual baseline DrQ+BC and DrQ-v2, so v2's consistent DrQ+BC naming does not establish a comparator replacement.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a proxy Q-error protocol comparing TD3+BC and pretrained TD3+BC trained on 10% of each dataset against a full-data TD3+BC reference critic. The removed online experiments also lose their one-million-interaction-step evaluation protocol. Retained offline training budgets, rollout schedules, and dataset-subsampling procedures are substantively unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Section 3.1 adds a nine-condition proxy Q-error analysis to investigate value-estimation accuracy under limited data. It removes the joint-loss design comparison and the analysis contrasting random-action versus pre-collected data for online pretraining. Existing rank, frozen-backbone, dataset-size, and restricted-state-coverage analyses remain, despite renumbering and relocation.

E5.justification: V2 Table 2 adds standard deviations for AWAC and previously unqualified IQL baseline scores. Conversely, its frozen-backbone table omits the CQL standard deviations present in v1 Table 7. V2's Robomimic Figure 5 newly states three seeds, while Appendix C still states five; an actual run-count change cannot be established consistently.

E6.justification: Baseline revisions materially change comparisons despite unchanged proposed-method D4RL scores. For example, AWAC medium-expert HalfCheetah changes from 36.8 to 76.4, with the proposed method at 90.1 in both versions. IQL medium Walker2d changes from 78.3 to 83.8 against unchanged 83.6, reversing the mean ranking. V2 also adds proxy errors, replaces and expands visual results, and removes online and joint-loss results.

T1.justification: V2 introduces a proxy Q-error definition by substituting a full-data TD3+BC critic for the unknown reference Q-function in the existing error expression. The finite, deterministic assumptions, linear decomposition, projected Bellman equation, and approximation bound remain unchanged, with v1 Equation 5 becoming v2 Equation 4. No new theorem or proof establishes improved rank or convergence.

C1.justification: The central claims of plug-and-play offline-RL improvement and strong performance with 10% of the data remain. V2 adds a more assertive theoretical contribution claim in the introduction: pretraining increases feature rank, tightens the error bound, and consequently improves convergence. This strengthens the conjectural mechanism explanation given in v1 Section 3.1.

C2.justification: V2 interprets its new proxy-error results as evidence of more accurate Q-function estimation and explicitly limits the design to model-free offline methods relying on Q-learning. It removes v1's explanation that random-action online pretraining can fail because limited state coverage increases dynamics uncertainty. Most interpretations of retained offline experiments remain substantively similar.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code access link for the proposed method, explicitly identifies backbone fine-tuning as the default, and specifies hard rather than soft rank for the existing rank analysis. Baseline repositories, offline training budgets, rollout counts, and RTX A5000 hardware information are largely retained. These disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including DR3, MOReL, prioritized-experience-replay studies, and masked trajectory models, and expands the online-versus-offline efficiency discussion in Appendix A. The existing comparisons with predictive representations, TD-MPC, JOWA, and Dreamer are retained and rewritten, moving from v1 Appendix F to v2 Appendix B.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation, experimental narrative, conclusion, and substantial appendix prose are extensively rewritten. V2 standardizes backbone/head terminology and reorganizes the appendices, including moving methodological discussion forward and repositioning implementation details and the frozen-backbone analysis. These changes substantially alter exposition and document structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn as an explicit two-stage workflow. V1's visual-benchmark bar chart becomes v2 Table 3, a proxy-error table is added, and the online/joint-loss tables are removed. Retained figures are resized or relocated, and several tables lose total rows. Most retained experimental plots display identical data despite changed numbering and captions.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the retained offline-RL contribution easier to understand and assess through clearer exposition, a redesigned workflow, fuller baseline comparisons, a code pointer, and additional diagnostic and visual results. The net gain is limited by removal of the joint-loss comparison and remaining reporting weaknesses. In particular, Table 3 claims consistent improvement despite two decreases, and the learned-critic proxy does not establish the stronger rank-to-convergence claims.
